name: Elasticities
description: How strongly one economic variable responds to a change in another.

name: Price elasticity of demand
description: How much quantity demanded responds to a change in the good's own price.

name: PED: definition
description: What PED measures and why it is a ratio of percentage changes.
intuition: If the price of your usual snack went up, would you still buy as many?

name: PED: formula and calculation
description: Calculating PED from percentage changes in quantity demanded and price.
intuition: If a 10% price rise cut your snack buying by 20%, how strongly did you react?

name: PED: interpreting values
description: Reading a PED value as elastic, inelastic or unit elastic, and what that means for total revenue.
intuition: Would you stop buying petrol if it cost a bit more? Would you stop buying one brand of crisps?

name: Price elasticity of supply
description: How much quantity supplied responds to a change in the good's own price.

name: PES: definition and determinants
description: What PES measures and what makes supply more or less elastic.
intuition: If strawberries suddenly sold for more, how fast could farmers grow extra?

name: PES: formula and calculation
description: Calculating PES from percentage changes in quantity supplied and price.
intuition: If a 10% higher price made a bakery bake 5% more bread, how strongly did it react?

name: Income elasticity of demand
description: How much quantity demanded responds to a change in consumers' income.

name: YED: definition and sign
description: What YED measures, and how its sign separates normal from inferior goods.
intuition: If you got a pay rise, what would you buy more of, and what less?

name: Indirect taxes and market failure
description: How taxes on goods change market outcomes and can correct market failure.

name: Incidence of an indirect tax
description: Who ends up paying an indirect tax: consumers or producers.

name: Indirect tax: shifting supply
description: Showing a specific or ad valorem tax as a shift of the supply curve on a diagram.
intuition: If a café had to pay 50p to the government on every coffee, what would happen to its prices?

name: Indirect tax: splitting the burden
description: Why the share of a tax paid by consumers depends on the price elasticities of demand and supply.
intuition: If a tax goes on something people can't do without, who ends up paying it?

name: Taxing negative externalities
description: Using a tax to make producers or consumers pay for external costs.

name: Evaluating taxes on negative externalities
description: Weighing how well a tax corrects an externality against problems such as valuing the external cost.
intuition: If a factory had to pay for the smoke it makes, would it make less?
